extraction.name: MATHVISTA
extraction.description: A benchmark designed to combine challenges from diverse mathematical and visual tasks. It consists of 6,141 examples, derived from 28 existing multimodal datasets involving mathematics and 3 newly created datasets (i.e., IQTest, FunctionQA, and PaperQA).
extraction.creator: Pan Lu, Hritik Bansal, Tony Xia, Jiacheng Liu, Chunyuan Li, Hannaneh Hajishirzi, Hao Cheng, Kai-Wei Chang, Michel Galley, Jianfeng Gao
extraction.rai:dataCollection: MATHVISTA incorporates 28 existing multimodal datasets, including 9 math-targeted question answering datasets and 19 VQA datasets. In addition, three new datasets (IQTest, FunctionQA, PaperQA) were created. For existing VQA datasets, heuristic rules automatically selected examples likely to involve mathematical reasoning, which were then manually labeled by three expert annotators. Each source dataset was limited to up to 400 examples.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Secondary Data analysis, Manual Human Curator
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Derived from 28 existing multimodal datasets and 3 newly created datasets. IQTest is sourced from puzzle test figures on online learning platforms. FunctionQA emphasizes functional plots. PaperQA is sourced from academic illustrations, including tables, figures, and charts from papers released in August 2023 on Huggingface.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Heuristic rules were initially designed to automatically select examples likely to involve mathematical reasoning from a large pool of candidates. Examples with numeric answers or those containing quantity words in the questions were selected. This automatic filtration yielded 4,949 VQA-format examples. Three expert annotators then manually labeled these examples. Each source dataset was limited to up to 400 examples to ensure a balanced representation.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: All questions for the new datasets were manually annotated by graduate students in STEM fields and further refined through a rigorous review process. Each dataset was independently annotated by three reviewers. Discrepancies were resolved through discussion among the entire review team, ensuring a consensus was reached on each example.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: The annotation process resulted in a high inter-annotation consistency rate of 99.2%. Among the newly collected 736 questions, only 6 exhibited disagreements, which were resolved through discussion. For the human labeling of mathematical problems, a Fleiss Kappa score of 0.775 was achieved, indicating a substantial level of consistency among the annotators.
extraction.rai:annotatorDemographics: Graduate students in STEM fields and expert annotators.
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The answer labels for the test set will not be publicly released to prevent data contamination. The creators will maintain an online evaluation platform and are committed to maintaining the datasets, refining potential data noise in response to community feedback, and evolving the leaderboard in response to new models.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The dataset facilitates the development of AI agents with strong mathematical reasoning capabilities in visual contexts, which have a wide range of real-world applications, such as solving complex problems in educational disciplines, helping analysts with logical queries about statistical data, and assisting in theorem proving and scientific discovery.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: Limitations include dataset coverage, as there may be gaps in the representation of certain types of mathematical problems and visuals. The scalability and generalizability to other domains remain a concern. Annotations sourced from original data providers lack a unified format and structure, and only 85.6% of examples have annotations.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Model development validation, standard evaluation, and benchmarking the mathematical and visual reasoning capabilities of Large Language Models (LLMs) and Large Multimodal Models (LMMs).
